content.value_statement: Vue projects often collect reactivity, component, and performance mistakes over time. This skill gives targeted Vue 3 guidance for safer patterns and clearer code.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Vue components for Composition API and script setup patterns.
Explains reactivity pitfalls involving refs, reactive objects, computed values, and watchers.
Guides Vue Router, Pinia, KeepAlive, Suspense, Teleport, and async component decisions.
Identifies performance risks in lists, transitions, scoped CSS, and render functions.
Provides TypeScript and SSR guidance for common Vue application structures.
limitations: It is reference guidance, not an automated linter or test runner.
It does not verify behavior without project files, runtime logs, or tests.
Some advice assumes Vue 3 and may need adjustment for Vue 2 projects.
It cannot replace framework security review for production applications.

use_cases.title: Review Vue Components
use_cases.description: Find reactivity, prop, emit, slot, and template issues before a pull request is merged.

use_cases.title: Plan Vue 3 Migration
use_cases.description: Move Options API code toward Composition API and script setup while preserving project behavior.

use_cases.title: Improve App Performance
use_cases.description: Diagnose watcher misuse, large list rendering, transition cost, and SSR hydration concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-best-practices to review this Vue component for Composition API, prop handling, and template issues. List the highest impact fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Options API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-best-practices to refactor this Options API component into Vue 3 script setup with TypeScript. Preserve behavior and explain compatibility risks.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-best-practices to diagnose reactivity, watcher, list rendering, and transition performance issues in this Vue feature. Recommend measured fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan SSR Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vue-best-practices to plan Vue SSR improvements for hydration, async components, and request-isolated state. Include tests and rollout checks.

output_examples.input: A component mutates props and performs filtering directly inside a template.
output_examples.output: The response highlights read-only prop rules, recommends emitted updates, and moves filtering into computed state for predictable rendering.

output_examples.input: A page uses deep watchers, large lists, and transitions that feel slow.
output_examples.output: The response separates watcher scope, list virtualization, stable props, and transform-based animations into prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A team wants to use SSR with shared state and async components.
output_examples.output: The response explains request-scoped stores, client-only API guards, hydration timing, and async component loading choices.

best_practices: Share the relevant Vue files and describe the current runtime behavior.
Ask for prioritized findings when reviewing large components or migrations.
Validate suggested changes with tests, type checks, and browser behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to enforce patterns without checking project conventions.
Do not copy examples without adapting them to your state model and routing setup.
Do not treat performance advice as proven without measuring the affected workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill support Vue 2?
faq.answer: It focuses on Vue 3. Some migration guidance covers Vue 2 differences, but Vue 3 patterns are the default.

faq.question: Can it review TypeScript Vue components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for defineProps, defineEmits, template refs, InjectionKey, and typed component refs.

faq.question: Does it run linting or tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that should be verified with your project lint, type check, and test commands.

faq.question: Can it help with SSR issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers shared state, platform-specific APIs, hydration timing, and server-rendered directive behavior.

faq.question: Is it useful for performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers large lists, watchers, computed values, transitions, scoped CSS, and rendering patterns.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
